0.original: Koana has the look of a man intent on finding bananas.

48.original: Spiced ibruq wrapped in najool leaves? That sounds like a winning combination to me!

49.original: Let us see if there are najool leaves to be had in town.

50.original: Perhaps the cook Urianger mentioned might be persuaded to spare us a few.

51.original: An underground oven! This must be the cook Urianger was talking about.

52.original: Hmm... The earth here is indeed fashioned into an oven of sorts. Fascinating.

53.original: Oh, hello again! Did you need something?

54.original: Najool leaves! For purposes <hex:021A020203>other<hex:021A020103> than xibruq pibil, naturally...

55.original: Unfortunately, I've just used up my last. You'll have to travel to the lower forests for more.

56.original: Golmajiik Grove is the source of the finest najool leaves you'll find. Wild variants you sometimes see in city markets can't compare.

57.original: I see... I had hoped to avoid such a lengthy venture, but if there's no other way to obtain our ingredient, then to the Ja Tiika Heartland we shall go.

58.original: Allow me to save you the trip.

59.original: Traveling there requires that you go through the Ty'iinbek Traverse, but it has caved in. Due to the recent storm, I expect.

60.original: What? But that means we can't get our najool leaves!

61.original: ...But we <hex:021A020203>can<hex:021A020103>, can't we? If there were no other way of procuring them, you would have suspended this feat, or else altered its objective.

63.original: Anyway, I apologize for the interruption, but having overheard your conversation, I felt compelled to chime in.

64.original: That's very kind of you. Any last-minute advice you'd be willing to share?

65.original: Only to undertake the Feat of Repast with an empty stomach. You may find xibruq pibil to be a delicious but daunting dish to finish.

67.original: Still...if there are no leaves here, and we can't travel for more, how are we supposed to gather all our ingredients?

68.original: These feats are meant to deepen our understanding of the peoples and cultures of Tuliyollal.

69.original: So perhaps there is something about xibruq pibil that we have yet to learn. Something of significance other than its recipe or ingredients.

70.original: Oh, I see... Like who was the first to make it─its history, that sort of thing!

71.original: Ahem! If it's Yak T'el's history you're interested in, you should start with the old war.

72.original: Between the Xbr'aal and the Mamool Ja, right?

73.original: These forests have borne witness to centuries of warfare, the evidence of which remains a scar upon the earth.

74.original: To know the end of that bloodshed is to know xibruq pibil.

75.original: Huh? What does steamed ibruq have to do with bloodshed?

76.original: Precisely the question we must answer. Vexing though such a detour may seem, I can think of no other way to approach this feat.

77.original: In that case, you may wish to visit the site of a settlement ruined by the war. The village of Ilyon Asoh─it lies a short distance to the east.

78.original: The village of Ilyon Asoh? Understood! Thank you for your help.

79.original: Come, let's go and see this place!

80.original: I was told not to talk about xibruq pibil. The history of our people and the─<cough>─<hex:021A020203>important developments therein<hex:021A020103> are another matter.

81.original: Everyone knows there was a war between the Mamool Ja and Xbr'aal. But I, uh...may have forgotten some of the details.

82.original: The village of Ilyon Asoh must be further east.

83.original: Let us continue with haste. For all we know, our competitors may be on our heels.

84.original: This place feels forgotten by time...

85.original: So this is the village of Ilyon Asoh...or what's left of it.

86.original: It was a place of light and life. My great-grandfather called it home, in fact.

87.original: Wuk Evu! I didn't know you were in Yak T'el!

88.original: I was picking up lumber from Iq Br'aax when I heard the Third Promise was on her way to this site of deep historical significance.

89.original: I immediately saw another opportunity to be of service, and so followed you here.

90.original: Wuk Evu is a shipwright who came to our aid during the Feat of Reeds.

91.original: A pleasure. You are a member of the Third Promise's retinue, I presume?

92.original: For the moment, I suppose I am. My name is Koana. Pleased to make your acquaintance.

93.original: Koana! Now that's a good name. A familiar name! Where have I heard...

94.original: Koana!? As in the Second Promise of Tuliyollal!?

95.original: To think that I addressed the Dawnservant's own son as some common retainer! Such disrespect cannot be excused. Please, take up your gun and─

96.original: Oh, come on, not this again!

97.original: I take no offense, so please do not dwell on it.

98.original: All right, then. I shan't dwell on it.

99.original: A-And right on cue... At least he's consistent?

100.original: I understand you wish to learn about xibruq pibil. While I am forbidden by the Xbr'aax Rax to divulge any information regarding its preparation, I would be happy to share what I know of Yak T'el's history.

102.original: In its most basic sense, the conflict between the Xbr'aal and Mamool Ja was one of land.

103.original: The Mamool Ja live in the lower forest, where the thick canopy obscures the sun and the soil is unforgiving to crops. This drove them to covet the upper forest─the home of the Xbr'aal─and they launched a determined campaign to seize it for themselves.

104.original: Yet advantage ever favors higher ground, and the Xbr'aal forces held the upper hand against the invaders, rebuffing them time and again.

105.original: But as the state of this village would attest, the tide eventually turned. What brought it about?

106.original: Something you know all too well: blessed siblings.

107.original: You must understand. The Mamool Ja were once a people as much at war with themselves as they were with others.

108.original: The Hoobigo, Boonewa, and Doppro each sought to assert dominance over the others, even as they engaged the Xbr'aal in battle.

109.original: In an effort to strengthen bonds and discourage infighting, Hoobigo and Boonewa leaders arranged a marriage between their children. However, this political measure altered the course of history in ways no one could have ever imagined.

110.original: It was long believed that partners of differing clans could not have children together.

111.original: But then it happened. A child arrived who shared the blood of Hoobigo and Boonewa both─a two-headed Mamool Ja.

112.original: Blessed with tremendous physical strength and magical prowess, he grew into a mighty warrior before eventually arising as the first Autarch─ruler of all three clans.

113.original: Such qualities would dispose anyone to leadership. Character notwithstanding.

114.original: Under the Autarch's rule, the newly united Mamool Ja became a force to be feared, and the war soon came to a head.

115.original: I think it best you see the results firsthand. Let us visit another battlefield from that time, and there I shall continue the tale.

118.original: I hope I have been of sufficient service to the Third Promise.

119.original: I never imagined our father was instrumental to xibruq pibil's invention...

120.original: Papa really did live up to his words. He traveled the land and learned about our people's myriad cultures.

121.original: And we're doing the same now...
